failures_and_fixes: Correction1 round: main review rejected CP01 (scaler hash+channels constructor bypassed provenance) and CP02 (mutable schema list changed a live builder allowlist); both were reproduced from the review document, fixed in the only public construction paths and locked by new regressions (28 tests total).

A PowerShell here-string patch attempt for the correction1 edits failed with the apply_patch wrapper (multi-line patch text through apply_patch.bat/cmd mangles embedded double quotes); nothing was written. All edits were then applied with the official codex apply_patch engine invoked from Python with the patch text as one exact argv element (apply_patch_safe.py and patch_*.txt, all embedded in the log), each returning success before any re-run.
Readback first pass this round failed exactly one stale self-check ('tests ran 23 tests'); it now expects the new 28-test count and the whole driver capture re-ran green.

First capture pass: tests exit 0 (Ran 23 tests OK) and FORCE exercise exit 0, but readback exit 1 with exactly two issues: (a) its 'module does not import causal_input' check was a substring test that the module docstring's legitimate cross-reference to ai_pc.model.causal_input (the distinct [1,13,32,1] sim_em_v2 summary profile) made fail; (b) it read manifest.json before the driver had written it. Fixed by (a) an AST-based stdlib import allowlist check plus 'causal_input not in imports' and (b) the driver writing manifest.json after every run; the whole capture was re-run: all three runs exit 0 and all 49 readback checks PASS.

A PowerShell here-string patch attempt for those two helper fixes produced literal backtick-escape text (single-quoted here-strings do not interpret backticks); it errored before any write, both helper files were re-read and confirmed unchanged, then rewritten wholesale and AST-gated before re-running.

The first ad-hoc column check used a naive '~A' prefix match that wrongly matched the '~Ascii' header, producing bogus all-NULL counts; corrected to exact section-header equality and captured as check_columns.py, whose counts then matched the exercise summary.

An early ad-hoc capture of check_columns and verify_scope used a PowerShell text redirect, which produced UTF-16LE bytes with a BOM; both were re-captured via Python subprocess capture_output (snippet executed via stdin, exact source saved as recapture_extra.py), the stale UTF-16 file was deleted, and the cited .bin captures are raw process bytes.

The captured column check was tightened once more for label hygiene: its intermediate variant classified every column via float() conversion; the final check_columns.py parses numbers only for depth + the four selected channels and classifies all other columns (including both label columns) by exact NULL-token match, and the capture was regenerated from that final source.
No other failures. The 23 unit tests passed in every formal capture run.
